intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Independence County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: On internal control, the auditors wrote: “During our audit we did not identify any deficiencies in internal control that we consider to be material weaknesses.”

limits: From the 2024 report, dated October 23, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Cushman
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor The governing body did not review the prior report and accompanying comments at the first regularly scheduled meeting following receipt of the report, as required by Ark. Code Ann. § 10-4-418.

cities.name: Magness
cities.quote: During our evaluation, noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor The Town entered into a seven year financing agreement, on August 14, 2024, in the amount of $41,506 to finance a tractor and attachments, which appears to be in conflict with Ark. Const. Amend, 78 § 2, limiting short-term financing obligations for a period not to exceed five years for the purpose of acquiring, constructing, installing, or renting real property or tangible property having a useful life of more than one year.
